doc.title: Dave Robinson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007

title: Reaching middle schools and young players
summary: The kit targets high school and college but includes an entry-level arrangement; Dave praises young players.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: What about junior high? Have you thought about that? I’m sure you probably did.

Well yes. I wanted this to really dig into the music and present — be like a textbook. I didn’t want to do like a calculus textbook that just shows you how to add two plus two equals four. So I wanted it to cover the whole thing and really get deep into it so the fact that it’s structured that way means it’s going to be applied mostly at the college and high school level. But I did include an entry level arrangement that I did for non-improvisers.
So I think middle schools could handle pieces of this and I hope they will. And in fact I’ve had some middle school directors asking me for this.

Well I mentioned it because my daughter teaches middle school music, and I’ve seen what’s going on in their district near Rochester, New York. And they’ve got kids in junior high that are playing jazz quite well, but in the big band experience. But these kids are standing up and taking solos — I’m not sure if their solos are worked out beforehand, some of them may be. But it’s quite amazing to see.

Yeah, oh there’s just some amazing young players out there, no doubt about it. I have the privilege of directing some of the best young players in the D.C. area in the Capital Focus Jazz Band and yeah, they constantly amaze me.
